# PR #861: Show a new chat in the sidebar while its first turn runs

- PR: https://github.com/EratoLab/erato/pull/861
- Status: pending (diff reviewed)
- Category: Bug fixes
- Theme: None

## Summary

**The PR's auto-generated description substantially undersells this
change** — it frames the PR mostly as "comprehensive end-to-end tests"
plus removing a redundant sidebar refresh, but the diff contains a
non-trivial new production feature: a sidebar "pending chat" placeholder
row, confirmed by reading `useChatHistory.ts` and `useChatMessaging.ts`
in full.

The underlying gap: the backend's `get_recent_chats` only returns chats
that already have a saved message, but the backend creates the chat row
(and emits `chat_created`) *before* the first user message is actually
saved — so between those two events, a brand-new chat had no way to
appear in the sidebar at all, and (per the PR title) could stay invisible
there for the whole duration of a slow first-turn generation.

Confirmed mechanism:
- A new `PendingChat` (`{ id, createdAt, assistantId? }`) is stored in
  `useChatHistoryStore` and set in `useChatMessaging.ts`'s
  `chat_created` handler — giving the sidebar something to render
  immediately, before the chat is listable.
- `useChatHistory`'s `chats` memo synthesizes a placeholder `RecentChat`
  row (empty title, `can_edit: false`, `last_selected_facets`/`last_model`
  deliberately left `undefined` so a real value from config isn't
  overridden by an absent one) and prepends it to the listed chats,
  *unless* the pending chat has already appeared in the real list.
- A `useEffect` clears the placeholder the moment the real row appears in
  the fetched list, "so a stale one would [not] re-appear as a ghost row
  the moment the real row leaves the list" (e.g. via archiving).
- The `user_message_saved` handler additionally triggers a **targeted**
  `refetchChatHistory()` specifically when the active stream is still
  showing a placeholder (`isPendingChat`), rather than after every
  message — confirmed via the code comment reasoning this avoids "one
  request per loaded page mid-stream" for every other, already-listed
  chat's turns.
- Every abandonment/error/close path (new-chat navigation, archive,
  stream error, resume-stream error, SSE close/error) explicitly calls
  `clearPendingChat()` so a first turn that never produces a listable
  message (aborted, errored, or interrupted) doesn't leave a permanent
  ghost placeholder — confirmed this is the mechanism the PR's own
  bullet-point test list ("Removing a pending chat before it's listed
  leaves no ghost row," "If the first turn ends before the message is
  saved, no ghost row remains") is actually testing, even though the
  description never explains *how* those guarantees are implemented.
- Separately, `Chat.tsx`'s `handleSendMessage` drops a now-redundant
  `refreshChats()` call after every send — confirmed correct given the
  new placeholder mechanism supersedes it for the new-chat case, and the
  existing chat case never needed a full refresh per PR #855's earlier fix.

## Compatibility and configuration

None. Pure frontend UX feature; no configuration or API changes. Behavior
change: starting a new chat now shows a placeholder row in the sidebar
immediately (title initially blank, filled in once the real chat is
listed), instead of the new chat being invisible in the sidebar until its
first message round-trip completes.

## Evidence and review

Verified via this PR's squash-merge commit against its parent (both
present locally). Read in full: the complete `useChatHistory.ts` diff
(the `PendingChat` type, store actions, placeholder-row synthesis, and
clearing effect) and the relevant `useChatMessaging.ts` diff (every call
site that sets or clears the pending placeholder across the chat-creation
and error/abort paths) and the `Chat.tsx` diff (the removed redundant
refresh). This is how the description's significant gap was found — its
bullet points describe only test coverage and a minor cleanup, prompting
direct verification of the much larger underlying feature the diff stat
revealed. Not read in full: the ~660 lines of new E2E specs
(`sidebar-new-chat.basic.spec.ts`, `sidebar-new-chat.many-models.spec.ts`)
or the 195-line `useChatHistory.test.ts` addition, though their described
scenarios align precisely with the mechanism verified in the production
code.

## Release note disposition

Proposed category: Bug fixes (arguably also Features and enhancements,
given the added placeholder UX). Worth a mention: starting a new chat now
shows it in the sidebar immediately, rather than only after its first
response begins saving — useful when the first turn takes a while to
generate.
